title: Pearl Harbor and war-time playing at army posts
summary: He recalls the WPA band at Jackson Barracks on Pearl Harbor Sunday and playing for soldiers and USO shows; he is not a sports fan.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Do you remember Pearl Harbor the day that happened?

I can tell you that I know that good as a book. We were playing at Jackson Barracks when I was in the WPA band. And you should have seen those soldiers' face how they changed because all of a while it was just draft. But then the country went into war then. Yeah, I was at WPA band. I was on a Sunday.
Sunday morning, I remember when that happened.
I was working at Crescent Bay, the country, the Gravid, and the country. I went home in 42. Did you go in the army? No. You played all during World War II?

Well yeah, at which they had to play, you know what I mean, because for a while they didn't have anything at all to play. Nobody was at the time, like I said, when I was in the WPA, because that's when we used to play the soldiers. We used to play the soldiers away from the parish prison, and then we used to play USO deals. But that was true at WPA. We played at Cavalier-Johnson, Jackson Barracks, up at Camp Prochet. We had a regular schedule with them, in a sense, I mean it was big.
You remember VE Day when Germany surrendered? No, I don't know. I can't really play. You can't recall. You remember when Japan? I can remember, but I can't remember what happened on the-

I just wondered if you remember who you were playing with. No, I can't remember. Do you follow boxing? Do you like boxing much? Do you remember where you were playing when different fights were, you know, like championships and all that?

No, I'll be frank with you. I never was much of a sports fan. I mean I enjoy a good fight or a good baseball game or any, even swimming, racing and so forth, but I would be an average sports fan I never was.
